body.objective: Add a proof-carrying global spectral layer for compact elliptic operators: domains, primed zero-mode deletion, resolvents, spectral measures, relative traces and determinants. Existing finite spectral/Jordan and local heat-kernel machinery does not determine the finite global form factors required by sf:program/work/quantum-background-specific-five-form-factor-spectral-realization. Conflux can discover local symbolic relations, but it must not interpolate global determinant data from round or product-space fixtures.
body.stop_condition: Define typed closed operators with Hilbert/Krein carrier declaration, domain, boundary conditions, adjoint/self-adjoint disposition, compact-resolvent evidence, orientation, measure, zero-mode projector and spectral cut. Provide exact finite-spectrum and certified-enclosure infinite-spectrum backends for resolvent matrix elements, contour or Mellin representations, primed heat traces, zeta/relative determinants, finite-rank and trace-class perturbation formulas, scale derivatives and local-versus-global subtraction data. Every finite part must name the common domain, projector and renormalization convention. Implement resolvent identities and determinant variation formulas with independent trace/spectral rails. Reproduce finite-matrix controls, the scalar circle/sphere spectra available exactly and one relative determinant with known answer; then realize or rigorously obstruct the five declared third-curvature form factors on one content-addressed non-round compact background. Export spectral projectors, poles, residues, enclosures and subtraction provenance through Conflux while marking finite global data as unavailable when only local symbols are known.
body.forbid: no local heat-kernel coefficient used as a finite determinant; no primed determinant without an explicit zero-mode projector; no relative determinant across different domains, measures or counterterm algebras; no truncated spectrum without a certified tail; no Euclidean spectral result promoted to Lorentzian causality or positivity; no Weyl-specific five-form-factor answer embedded in lib/math; no Conflux interpolation from special backgrounds called a universal result
notes: Priority 3. This is distinct from M14a's rational/log/polylog and integration-by-parts work: it supplies the missing global operator datum.
The first useful slice can be compact one-dimensional and separable homogeneous operators plus finite-rank perturbations, followed by a general receiver interface.
The key adoption rule is negative as well as positive: Conflux must be able to prove that local symbol data underdetermines a finite spectral quantity.
